Determining your personality type can be done through several methods. One popular and widely used method is the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI), which categorizes people based on preferences in four areas:

1. **Extraversion (E) vs Introversion (I):** This refers to your energy sources. Extraverts get energized by being with others and tend to focus outward, while introverts recharge alone and tend to focus inward.
   
2. **Sensing (S) vs Intuition (N):** This deals with how you take in information. Sensing individuals prefer using past experiences and current data to make decisions, whereas intuitive individuals focus on abstract possibilities and future trends.

3. **Thinking (T) vs Feeling (F):** This relates to decision-making style. Thinkers make choices based on logic and facts, while feelers base their decisions on feelings and ethical considerations.

4. **Judging (J) vs Perceiving (P):** This pertains to how you organize your life. Judgers prefer structure and making decisions, while perceiving individuals enjoy flexibility and prefer to absorb new information before acting.

Using these four categories, you can match your preferences to one of the 16 personality types. Each combination of preferences is considered an individual personality type within the MBTI framework.
